question: Can a Gaussian-process surrogate and exploration-oriented experimental design efficiently expose which researcher choices make machine-learning conclusions change?

key_findings.claim: The proposed machine-learning multiverse replaces exhaustive evaluation of a declared decision space with a Gaussian-process surrogate sampled to reduce integrated posterior variance.
key_findings.evidence: The framework requires a search space and evaluation function, begins with a Sobol design, fits a Matérn-5/2 ARD GP, and acquires batches by Monte Carlo integrated variance reduction rather than performance optimization. Posterior surfaces, additive-versus-shared-kernel Bayes factors, and variance-based sensitivity indices summarize the explored space.

key_findings.claim: A toy SVM example demonstrates the descriptive advantage of exploration over optimization, but its fairness illustration is synthetic rather than evidence about an observed protected group.
key_findings.evidence: From a common initial design, UCB and IVR each add 23 configurations. IVR reveals a broad accuracy plateau in C-gamma space, along which an independently sampled Bernoulli group label appears to have different outcome gaps; no real demographic variable or fairness intervention is evaluated.

key_findings.claim: In the VGG-16/CIFAR-10 optimizer case study, matched learning rate almost entirely determines the observed SGD-minus-Adam difference, whereas Adam epsilon contributes little in the sampled box.
key_findings.evidence: Across three batches of 32 points after the initial design, the GP surface favors SGD through most of the middle learning-rate range but Adam at low and high extremes. Learning-rate main sensitivity is 0.990 plus or minus 0.014, epsilon is approximately zero, and an additive-kernel Bayes factor of 2635 argues against an interaction in this restricted two-dimensional multiverse.

key_findings.claim: The optimizer comparison does not establish a generally fair optimizer ranking because the two methods share one learning-rate coordinate while their other consequential hyperparameters and broader tasks are not independently tuned.
key_findings.evidence: The search holds SGD momentum and Adam beta values fixed, applies epsilon only to Adam, uses one VGG/CIFAR-10 setting, and evaluates pointwise differences at a common learning rate. The discussion itself says the multiverse should be expanded to every architecture, dataset, framework, and optimizer variant in the source claim.

key_findings.claim: On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, retained runs show a diagonal plateau consistent with increasing learning rate with batch size, but more than half of all trials are excluded and Tiny ImageNet entirely fails as a test of the claimed relation.
key_findings.evidence: The study evaluates 224 configurations across learning rate, batch size, three architectures, and three datasets, then drops 9 failed trials and 115 more with training accuracy below 0.99. Of 42 Tiny ImageNet runs, 22 meet that training threshold but none exceed 0.01 test accuracy. The plotted CIFAR surfaces support a plateau; the paper acknowledges some contours disagree with raw points because the coregionalized GP shares information.

key_findings.claim: The evidence for a learning-rate-by-batch-size interaction is suggestive, not conclusive enough to support an unrestricted claim that the pattern holds irrespective of model and dataset.
key_findings.evidence: The reported additive-versus-shared Bayes factor is 0.58, or 0.34 after removing Tiny ImageNet, while individual main sensitivities are 0.03 plus or minus 0.06 for learning rate and 0.02 plus or minus 0.06 for batch size. Dataset sensitivity is 0.83 plus or minus 0.03, dominated by the failed Tiny ImageNet condition, and the conclusion is empirically supported on only two of three datasets.

key_findings.claim: Adaptive use of test accuracy, single-seed evaluations, and conditioning on successful optimization weaken the framework's confirmatory interpretation even though the paper is candid about several of these limitations.
key_findings.evidence: Test accuracy is the acquisition target in every example, so repeated GP-guided decisions consume test-set feedback. Each configuration is trained once under a homoscedastic observation model, and large-batch analysis conditions on training accuracy at least 0.99. The authors explicitly propose heteroscedastic repeated evaluation, preregistration, larger search spaces, and new visualizations as future work.

method.core_idea: Treat plausible experimental choices as coordinates of a multiverse, approximate outcome surfaces with a GP, and spend compute where it most reduces global uncertainty rather than where performance seems maximal.
method.mechanism: Declare X and an outcome function; sample Sobol points; fit noisy single- or multi-output GPs; acquire batches by integrated variance reduction; then inspect mean and variance surfaces, compare kernels by marginal likelihood, and estimate global sensitivities.
assumptions: The declared dimensions, bounds, outcome, and kernel cover the scientifically relevant researcher choices.
A smooth stationary GP with the selected noise model is an adequate surrogate for discontinuous training failures and heterogeneous variance.
Integrated variance reduction explores the regions needed for the downstream interaction and robustness questions.
Repeated adaptive consultation of test accuracy does not invalidate the intended scientific generalization claim.
Discarding runs below a training-accuracy threshold isolates generalization without changing the estimand in a misleading way.

techniques.role: Interpolates an expensive outcome across continuous and categorical researcher-choice dimensions.
Provides low-discrepancy initial coverage before adaptive sampling.
Chooses experiments to reduce uncertainty throughout the multiverse rather than maximize accuracy.
Uses marginal-likelihood comparison of additive and shared kernels as evidence about interactions.
Shares statistical strength across architecture and dataset outputs in the batch-size case study.
Separates main and total effects under the fitted surrogate.

evaluations.setting: RBF SVM on Wisconsin Breast Cancer data
evaluations.metric: test accuracy surface after 23 acquired configurations
evaluations.result: IVR exposes a broad C-gamma plateau hidden by UCB's optimization-focused sample pattern.
evaluations.baseline: Upper-confidence-bound acquisition from the same initial sample.

evaluations.setting: VGG-16 with batch normalization and dropout on CIFAR-10
evaluations.result: SGD wins through much of the mid learning-rate range, Adam wins in some extremes, and learning rate explains almost all fitted output variance.
evaluations.baseline: Pointwise matched optimizer runs across learning rate and Adam epsilon; no independent per-optimizer tuning budget.

evaluations.setting: AlexNet, VGG-16, and ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet
evaluations.metric: test accuracy conditional on training accuracy at least 0.99
evaluations.result: A learning-rate/batch-size plateau appears for the two CIFAR datasets; every Tiny ImageNet run has test accuracy at most 0.01 and 124 of 224 total runs are discarded or fail.
evaluations.baseline: GP additive-versus-shared-kernel comparison and raw correlations, without repeated seeds or a reserved confirmatory test set.

limitations: The search space, its boundaries, the response, the surrogate, and the acquisition function remain additional researcher choices rather than a complete enumeration of the multiverse.
All configurations use one seed and a homoscedastic noise model, so training variance is not separated from configuration effects.
Adaptive acquisition directly optimizes information about test accuracy, creating sequential test-set reuse unless a final untouched set is reserved.
Removing every run below 0.99 training accuracy discards more than half the large-batch study and conditions conclusions on optimization success.
A multi-output GP can create smooth cross-dataset contours unsupported by nearby observations, especially when one dataset completely fails.
The 1,138 GPU-hour illustrative analysis still covers few architectures, datasets, schedules, stopping rules, optimizers, and metrics.
failure_modes: The GP smooths over sharp instability or training-failure boundaries and reports a reassuring plateau.
Adaptive test-set reuse promotes a multiverse conclusion that does not survive a newly collected or held-out test set.
A success filter removes configurations where the purported scaling rule fails, converting an end-to-end robustness question into a conditional one.
Coregionalization borrows signal from easier datasets to fill an unsupported surface for a failed dataset.
A weak marginal-likelihood preference is narrated as decisive evidence for or against an interaction.
Changing bounds, kernels, outcome metrics, random seeds, or termination criteria reverses the inferred robust region.
reusable_insights: Global exploration is the right objective when the scientific target is a response surface rather than a winning configuration.
Training failures are substantive outcomes in a robustness analysis and should be modeled, not silently conditioned away.
Pair every adaptively explored test surface with a frozen protocol and an untouched confirmatory dataset.
Use replicated seeds and a heteroscedastic or hierarchical surrogate to distinguish configuration effects from run variance.
Publish raw observations, uncertainty surfaces, acquisition history, and sensitivity to the multiverse definition alongside visual conclusions.
open_questions: How should failed and censored training runs be jointly modeled with continuous performance without distorting the target claim?
Can multiverse acquisition optimize the probability of resolving a prespecified claim rather than integrated variance alone?
How stable are conclusions to alternative kernels, priors, bounds, seed allocation, and categorical-output structures?
What sequential testing or reusable-holdout procedure preserves confirmatory validity under adaptive multiverse exploration?
Can compute be allocated between new configurations and repeats using estimated heteroscedastic noise and decision value?

competitive_landscape.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
competitive_landscape.difference: Bouthillier et al. explicitly model data, initialization, and hyperparameter sources of benchmark variance and quantify error in detecting improvements. The multiverse paper maps configuration response surfaces but evaluates each point once and cannot separate seed noise from choice effects.

competitive_landscape.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science
competitive_landscape.difference: Kapoor and Narayanan document leakage across 329 papers and propose reporting controls. Their taxonomy makes the multiverse framework's adaptive use of test accuracy a validity issue that exploration coverage alone cannot solve.

competitive_landscape.title: On Empirical Comparisons of Optimizers for Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Choi et al. show optimizer rankings can reverse with tuning protocols and emphasize independent search spaces and inclusion relations. The multiverse case gives a useful surface view but compares optimizers at matched learning rates in one restricted task.

competitive_landscape.title: On Large-Batch Training for Deep Learning: Generalization Gap and Sharp Minima
competitive_landscape.difference: Keskar et al. report a large-batch generalization gap and connect it empirically to sharper solutions. The multiverse paper challenges universality of that result by jointly varying learning rate, but only on retained successful runs and two functioning datasets.

competitive_landscape.title: Accurate, Large Minibatch SGD: Training ImageNet in 1 Hour
competitive_landscape.difference: Goyal et al. demonstrate linear learning-rate scaling plus warmup at ImageNet scale and batches up to 8,192. The multiverse analysis systematically visualizes a related diagonal plateau, but its Tiny ImageNet experiments fail and omit warmup and schedule dimensions.

competitive_landscape.title: Making Uncertainty Visible: Multiverse Analysis for Robust Computational Social Science
competitive_landscape.difference: Linde et al. apply multiverse analysis to modern computational social-science workflows and foreground failed methodological combinations and defensible-choice communication. That later emphasis directly addresses the present paper's exclusion of failures and the interpretive burden of large computational multiverses.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after full-text and current primary-source comparison: the paper makes a useful methodological contribution by marrying multiverse reasoning to exploration-oriented GP experimental design, and its response-surface visualizations are more informative than winner-only tuning. It does not by itself make the case studies confirmatory or generally robust: single runs, adaptive test-set reuse, a severe success filter, a completely failed dataset, and modest interaction evidence leave the empirical conclusions narrower than the rhetoric.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed all 20 pages, including method equations, both case studies, raw-count disclosures, compute accounting, future-work caveats, and appendix references. Six directly relevant primary arXiv papers were checked on 2026-08-23; audit distinguishes the framework's exploratory value from the validity of its case-study claims.
